name: Darwin Robotics
long_description:
Darwin Robotics is building general-purpose robot technicians that assemble and maintain the machines civilization runs on.

We're starting with AI infrastructure, automating physical work across data center assembly, commissioning, and maintenance. Our robots learn complex tasks from human demonstrations and improve through real-world deployment.

Initial deployments targeted for early 2027.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We are brothers and have been building things together our whole lives. We grew up in the Caribbean with our mom, obsessed with math and computers. Sergio taught himself calculus from MIT OpenCourseWare at 12, published mathematics as a teenager, and later worked on AI and robotics at Stanford, Nvidia, and Google X. Luigi studied math and CS at Columbia, then co-founded a payments company where he scaled engineering from zero to billions in transaction volume.

As kids, we built worlds in Minecraft. Now, we’re building robots.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Since antiquity, humans have invented tools and machines to advance civilization. We believe the next industrial revolution will come from intelligent machines that can themselves build and maintain other machines.

By bringing intelligence and dexterity into the physical world, robots will accelerate technological progress and expand what humanity can build beyond the limits of human labor.

To build new cities, expand industry, and eventually establish civilization beyond Earth, humanity will need more than its own hands.

launches.title: Darwin Robotics: Robot technicians for AI infrastructure
launches.tagline: General-purpose robot technicians that assemble, commission, and maintain data centers.
launches.body:
Hey YC,

We're Sergio and Luigi, co-founders of[ Darwin Robotics](https://darwinrobotics.ai/) (YC F25).

## **TL;DR**

We're building **general-purpose robot technicians that assemble, commission, and maintain data centers.**

Our mission: **Robots to build civilization.**

Our robots learn complex physical tasks from human demonstrations and improve through real-world deployment.

**Our ask:** We're looking for data center operators interested in deploying robot technicians. If you work in this space or can make an introduction, reach out at [sergio@darwinrobotics.ai](mailto:sergio@darwinrobotics.ai).

<https://youtu.be/3r9rG1-NwPw>

## **The Problem: Compute Is Scaling. Physical Work Isn't.**

Global data center capacity is projected to nearly double by 2030, from 103 to 200 gigawatts.

But bringing that much compute online requires an enormous amount of physical work. Skilled technicians must install servers, connect electrical and fiber cables, and commission the infrastructure. Once operational, these facilities require ongoing maintenance and repair.

As AI infrastructure scales, this physical work becomes a bottleneck in time-to-compute.

## **Our Solution**

Our vision is a robot technician that can take a work order and execute the physical tasks required to assemble, configure, and repair hardware.

That could mean installing hundreds of fiber optic connections, replacing a failed server component, or assembling new hardware, all with the same robot.

Rather than explicitly programming each workflow, our robots learn from human demonstrations.

We're a deployment-first company. We start with human supervision, collect demonstrations, corrections, and failures, and use that data to improve our models. As reliability improves, we progressively reduce supervision toward full autonomy.

The demo above shows our robot performing learned cable manipulation on a server rack.

We're targeting initial deployments in early 2027.

## **Why We Started Darwin**

We're brothers who grew up in the Caribbean, building things together and obsessed with math and computers. As kids, we built worlds in Minecraft. Now, we're building robots.

Before Darwin, Sergio worked on AI and robotics research at Stanford, Google X, and NVIDIA. Luigi founded and scaled a fintech payments company processing billions in transaction volume.

Throughout history, humans have advanced civilization by using tools to build increasingly sophisticated machines. We believe the next industrial revolution will come from intelligent machines that can themselves build and maintain other machines.

We're starting by bringing that capability to the infrastructure powering AI.

## **Our Ask**

We're already in discussions with hyperscalers and data center operators about initial deployments.

**If you're building or operating data centers, we'd love to explore deploying Darwin at your facilities.**

We're particularly interested in introductions to data center engineering, operations, and commissioning teams.

Contact: [ask@darwinrobotics.ai](mailto:ask@darwinrobotics.ai)

Website:[ ](https://darwinrobotics.ai/)[darwinrobotics.ai](http://darwinrobotics.ai)

## **The Founders**

**Sergio Charles (CEO):** Previously worked on AI and robotics research at Stanford, Google X, and NVIDIA, including robot learning research with Chelsea Finn and computer vision research with Andrew Ng. Stanford B.S. Mathematics & Computer Science, M.S. Statistics.

**Luigi Charles (CTO):** Previously founded and scaled Sphere, a fintech payments startup processing billions in transaction volume. Columbia B.S. Computer Science & Mathematics.

We're based in San Francisco.
